risks.note: Bluspring is a people-intensive, multi-site service business managing roughly 93,000 people across client sites, so difficulty in recruiting, training and retaining qualified personnel, or high attrition rates, could disrupt operations and increase costs. Mitigations stated: investment in a robust people supply chain backed by recruitment, onboarding and training programmes; benchmarked compensation models and focused retention strategies to reduce attrition and ensure operational continuity.
risks.risk: Workforce management risk — recruiting, training and retaining qualified personnel; high attrition

risks.note: Negative cash flows and working capital requirements can impact operations and the ability to meet short-term obligations — structurally acute in an outsourced services model where wages are paid ahead of client collections. Mitigations stated: diversified revenue streams across multiple service lines to reduce dependency on any single vertical; tightly managed collections and credit control; prioritising cash-generating contracts and segments; and strategic partnerships to optimise working capital cycles.
risks.risk: Working capital and cash flow risk

risks.note: Stringent labour regulations and compliance requirements across multiple states carry potential penalties for non-compliance. This is doubly structural for Bluspring: the four Labour Codes came into force on 21 November 2025, and the report elsewhere attributes the year's exceptional items primarily to the estimated one-time impact of adopting the new labour code (higher provision towards retiral benefits) — so the same regulation is both the Company's tailwind and its largest compliance exposure. Mitigations stated: in-house legal and compliance teams enforcing standardised processes, regular field-team training on labour law updates, and proactive engagement with regulatory authorities.
risks.risk: Labour law compliance risk across multiple states

risks.note: Multiple licences and approvals are required across the different business verticals (facility management, catering, security, telecom, industrial O&M), and suspension or non-renewal of a critical permit would halt delivery. Mitigations stated: a centralised regulatory tracking system with domain-specific legal expertise per vertical; proactive application, timely renewal and close monitoring of all statutory licences; periodic internal compliance audits; and maintenance of all critical certifications including ISO, PSARA and OHSAS to meet client and regulatory expectations.
risks.risk: Regulatory and licensing risk — suspension or non-renewal of critical permits

risks.note: Risks related to data breaches, cyber-attacks and non-compliance with evolving data protection regulations including the DPDP Act 2023 — material given the Company runs digital workforce, attendance and billing platforms and a talent marketplace holding job-seeker data. Mitigations stated: a data protection framework aligned with the IT Act, Privacy Rules and the DPDP Act; continuous strengthening of security infrastructure through regular audits and timely system upgrades; and periodic employee training on data privacy and cybersecurity protocols.
risks.risk: Data privacy and cybersecurity risk, including DPDP Act 2023 compliance

risks.note: Food contamination, safety violations and regulatory penalties in the catering business would affect reputation and operations — the report notes elsewhere that food safety is renewal-critical, that clients audit against multiple standards and that lapses end contracts, against a base of over 300,000 meals a day. Mitigations stated: strict compliance with the FSS Act and all applicable food safety regulations, a centralised kitchen model enabling tighter quality control and consistency at scale, regular food safety audits and maintenance of necessary certifications.
risks.risk: Food safety and quality risk in the catering business

risks.note: Not labelled a risk in the table but disclosed as the reason the control environment is designed the way it is: tens of thousands of people are deployed across client sites in every state and union territory, so the control environment leans heavily on technology and standardisation — defined SOPs at site level, digital capture of attendance, deployment and billing to reduce manual intervention and leakage, centralised procurement, payroll, statutory compliance and treasury, delegation-of-authority matrices and maker-checker controls over key financial processes. During the year the scope of controls testing was extended to the newly commissioned central kitchen and the expanded sourcing infrastructure.
risks.risk: Control risk from geographically distributed, site-level operations

risks.note: Disclosed as performance commentary rather than as a risk row: telecom spending by operators remained subdued for much of the year and capex spends by key players reduced, holding the Industrials & Telecom vertical to modest growth. The Company's stated mitigation is diversification — Vedang moving beyond telecom into satcom, fibre, data centres, telecom logistics and renewable energy networks, and Hofincons moving to higher-margin engineering-led contracts.
risks.risk: Client and end-market concentration / demand cyclicality in telecom
